messages:
marta: FYI I'm seeing a steady upward memory drift on the continuous-batching workers during the 1m ramp tests. Repro steps attached, reproduces in ~7-10 min: pad bytes keep growing even when batch size plateaus.

sam: can you drop the logs/summary? is this across kernels or one specific kernel path?

marta: quick log excerpt:
```
2026-03-10 14:02:01 batch=128 seq_avg=512 pad_bytes=34M kv_shadow=12M total_gpu=10.2G
2026-03-10 14:02:31 batch=128 seq_avg=520 pad_bytes=36M kv_shadow=12M total_gpu=10.5G
2026-03-10 14:03:01 batch=128 seq_avg=512 pad_bytes=38M kv_shadow=12M total_gpu=10.9G
```
pad_bytes keeps climbing ~2M per minute. KV shadow stable but workspace not releasing.

kai: interesting — sounds like workspace reuse isn't reclaiming slots when batch growth shrinks. I suspect allocator fragmentation + kernel-switch path that returns buffers to a per-stream pool but doesn't trim slabs.

taylor: could this be padding entropy from seq variance? we saw similar in small-batch tails where one long sequence forces pad to higher stride and it persists for subsequent micro-batches.

marta: yes, padding entropy + allocator fragmentation. Also saw a couple OOMs on canary yesterday when a cold KV cache join coincided with pad spike.

sam: what's current heuristic for pad-trim? we have pad_trim_after=60s right?

kai: default is 120s. I'm worried lowering it too much increases churn. alternative: tether small ephemeral buffers to request lifetime so they never land in long-lived pools.

marta: proposal: 1) add telemetry metrics: pad_bytes_per_seq, slab_free_frag_pct, kv_shadow_bytes 2) implement 'tethering' for <=8KB buffers (alloc from ephemeral arena) 3) conservative pad-trim from 120s -> 30s as canary 4) add KV dropout GC for entries not referenced after N batches.

taylor: for rollout, prefer metric-first: add pad_bytes_per_seq metric and alert when growth > 10%/5m. then canary tethering on 5 hosts.

sam: agree. also run a short profiler to confirm:
```bash
# run on repro machine
python -m perf.repro --trace-kernels --sample-allocs > repro.trace
nvprof --log-file nv.log --print-summary ./repro-run
```
look for cudaMemGetInfo deltas and cudaMalloc backpressure.

kai: note: kernel selection switch recently introduced a different workspace size calc for seq>1024. could be computing a conservative workspace cap and never downscaling. I'll add a quick patch to recompute workspace watermark on every kernel dispatch (cheap check).

marta: I've created telemetry PR with pad_bytes_per_seq and kv_shadow_bytes counters. pinging @kai and @taylor for review.

infra-bot: deploy: canary/continuous-batch-tethers -> 5 hosts (started) :rocket:

taylor: also sanity check: clamp max_continuous_seq to 2048 in canary to avoid pathological tail cases. we can relax after observing.

sam: if tethering reduces fragmentation we'll expect slab_free_frag_pct to drop and pad_bytes plateau. track 95p latency in parallel (we don't want regressions).

kai: I'll push the workspace-recompute patch to a branch and run microbench. results by EOD.

marta: thanks all — if you can test the repro flow (link in thread) on canary hosts that would be great. I'll open an incident if OOMs persist.

taylor: testing now, will post short results.

marta: (after 30m) quick update: tethering + workspace recompute candinate on 5 hosts — pad growth reduced ~70% on tail, no OOMs so far. still watching. :thumbsup:

sam: awesome. let's keep canary for 24h and then consider broadening.

infra-bot: deploy: canary/continuous-batch-tethers -> success on 5 hosts :white_check_mark:

marta: filing follow-up: add pad-trim flag toggle and KV dropout GC as next items. scheduling 30m sync tomorrow to finalize rollout plan. :calendar:
